u1-l01-s01.text: The board has 64 squares: 8 files and 8 ranks, in alternating colors.

u1-l01-s02.text: Files are named with letters, from a to h. Ranks are named with numbers, from 1 to 8. White starts at the bottom.

u1-l01-s03.text: Each square is named by its file and its rank. The highlighted one is e4: file e, rank 4.

u1-l01-s04.text: A handy trick: the bottom-right corner square, h1, is always light.

u1-l01-s05.hint: File e, fourth rank counting from the bottom.

u1-l01-s08.prompt: What is the highlighted square called?
u1-l01-s08.explanation: It's on file f and rank 3: f3.

u1-l01-s09.prompt: What is the highlighted square called?
u1-l01-s09.explanation: It's on file b and rank 6: b6.

u1-l02-s01.text: The rook moves in straight lines: along files and ranks, as many squares as it likes.

u1-l02-s02.text: It can't jump over other pieces. If it runs into an enemy piece, it can capture it and stops there.

u1-l02-s03.hint: Move it to the right along rank 4.

u1-l02-s05.prompt: Capture the black pawn with the rook.
u1-l02-s05.hint: It's on the same file as your rook.

u1-l03-s01.text: The bishop moves diagonally, as many squares as it likes, without jumping over pieces.

u1-l03-s02.text: Each bishop always stays on squares of the same color. That's why you start with two: one on light squares and one on dark squares.

u1-l03-s03.hint: Go up the diagonal to the right.

u1-l03-s04.hint: Go down the diagonal to the left.

u1-l03-s05.prompt: Capture the black pawn with the bishop.
u1-l03-s05.hint: It's on the diagonal, one square up and to the right.

u1-l04.title: The queen
u1-l04.summary: A rook and a bishop in one piece

u1-l04-s01.text: The queen moves like a rook and a bishop combined. It's the most powerful piece.

u1-l04-s02.text: The white queen starts on a light square and the black queen on a dark one. Take good care of it: losing your queen often decides the game.

u1-l04-s04.hint: Move it in a straight line along rank 4.

u1-l04-s05.prompt: Capture the black pawn with the queen.
u1-l04-s05.hint: It's right next to the queen, on the right.

u1-l05-s01.text: The king moves one square in any direction. It's the most important piece: if you lose it, you lose the game.

u1-l05-s02.text: The king can never move to a square attacked by the opponent. Here the black rook controls the d-file and rank 2.

u1-l05-s04.prompt: Move the king to a safe square.

u1-l05-s05.prompt: Can the king go to d3?
options: No, the rook attacks that square
u1-l05-s05.explanation: The black rook controls the whole d-file.

u1-l06-s01.text: The knight moves in an L shape: two squares in one direction and one to the side.

u1-l06-s02.text: It's the only piece that jumps over others. Here it's surrounded by pawns and it can still move.

u1-l06-s03.hint: Two squares to the right and one up.

u1-l06-s04.hint: Two squares down and one to the left.

u1-l06-s05.prompt: Capture the black pawn with the knight.
u1-l06-s05.hint: Two to the right and one up.

u1-l07.title: The pawn
u1-l07.summary: Moves straight, captures diagonally and promotes

u1-l07-s01.text: The pawn moves one square forward. On its first move it can advance two.

u1-l07-s02.text: After that first move, it can only advance one square.

u1-l07-s03.text: The pawn captures diagonally, one square forward.

u1-l07-s04.text: It doesn't capture straight ahead: if a piece is in front of it, the pawn is blocked.

u1-l07-s06.prompt: Capture one of the black pawns.

options: No, there's a piece in front of it
u1-l07-s07.explanation: The pawn can't advance or capture straight ahead.

u1-l07-s08.text: When a pawn reaches the last rank, it promotes: it turns into a queen, rook, bishop or knight, whichever you choose. The queen, the strongest piece, is almost always the right choice.

u1-l07-s09.prompt: Promote the pawn and choose the queen.
u1-l07-s09.hint: Advance the pawn to d8 and tap the queen in the selector.
u1-l07-s09.success: Correct. The pawn is now a queen.

u1-l07-s10.text: The queen isn't always best. Here, if you promote to a queen, Black plays Qc1+: your new queen has to block on e1, it gets captured, and it's mate.

u1-l07-s11.prompt: Promote the pawn in a way that wins the black queen.
u1-l07-s11.hint: A knight on e8 would check the king and attack the queen at the same time.
u1-l07-s11.success: Correct. The knight checks the king and attacks the queen: after the check, you capture it.

u1-l07-s12.text: The king steps aside and the knight captures the queen. Promoting to a piece other than a queen is called underpromotion.

u1-l08-s01.text: The knight is protected by the pawn: if the bishop captures it, the pawn recaptures. That's what protecting means.

u1-l08-s02.text: Now nothing protects the knight. If the bishop captures it, you lose it for nothing. A piece like that is called hanging.

u1-l08-s03.explanation: No white piece defends it, so the bishop captures it for free.

u1-l08-s04.prompt: Protect the knight with the rook.
u1-l08-s04.hint: Move the rook so that it sees the square d4.

u1-l08-s05.prompt: Capture the black piece that isn't protected.
u1-l08-s05.hint: The bishop is protected by a pawn.

u1-l09-s01.text: A trade happens when you capture and your opponent recaptures. To decide if it's worth it, add up the points: pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9.

u1-l09-s02.text: If the rook captures this pawn, the pawn on c6 recaptures. You win 1 point and lose 5: that's a bad trade.

u1-l09-s03.text: Here your pawn captures a knight. If the pawn on c6 recaptures, you've won 3 points and lost 1: that's a good trade.

u1-l09-s04.prompt: Is it worth capturing the pawn with the rook?
options: No, I lose the rook for a pawn

u1-l09-s05.prompt: Is it worth capturing the knight with your pawn?
options: Yes, I win a knight for a pawn
u1-l09-s05.explanation: You win 3 points and, even if they recapture, you only lose 1.
feedback: True, they can recapture, but the knight is worth more than the pawn.

u1-l09-s06.prompt: There's a black pawn on d5. Which piece should capture it?
u1-l09-s06.explanation: The pawn: if the black queen recaptures, your queen takes it.
feedback: With the queen, the queens get traded. There's a better option.

u1-l09-s07.text: Look at the sequence: the pawn captures, the black queen recaptures, and your queen takes the black queen. You win 9 points for a pawn.

u1-l10.title: Check
u1-l10.summary: When the king is under attack

u1-l10-s01.text: Check means the king is attacked by an enemy piece. Here the white rook gives check to the black king.

u1-l10-s02.text: The king is never captured. If it's in check, its owner has to get out of check on the very next move.

u1-l10-s03.prompt: Give check to the black king with the rook.

u1-l10-s04.prompt: Give check to the black king with the knight.
u1-l10-s04.hint: Find a square from which the knight attacks e8.

u1-l10-s05.prompt: Is the black king in check?
u1-l10-s05.explanation: The rook attacks rank 2 and the a-file, not the king.

u1-l10-s06.prompt: Is the black king in check?
u1-l10-s06.explanation: The rook attacks along the e-file and nothing stands in between.

u1-l11.title: Getting out of check
u1-l11.summary: Three ways to save the king

u1-l11-s01.text: If your king is in check, you have to get out of it. First way: move the king to a square that isn't attacked.

u1-l11-s02.text: Second way: block the attack by putting a piece in between.

u1-l11-s03.text: Third way: capture the piece giving check.

u1-l11-s04.prompt: Block the check with the knight.
u1-l11-s04.hint: Put the knight on the e-file, between the rook and the king.

u1-l11-s05.prompt: With the bishop, capture the piece giving check.
u1-l11-s05.hint: The attacker is the white knight.

u1-l11-s06.prompt: Move the king to a safe square.
u1-l11-s06.hint: The rook controls all of rank 8.

u1-l11-s07.text: If none of the three options works, there's no way out: that's checkmate. We'll look at it in the next lesson.

u1-l12-s01.text: Checkmate: the king is in check and has no way out. The game ends and whoever gave mate wins. Here the black king is boxed in by its own pawns.

u1-l12-s02.text: The queen gives check and the white king protects it, so the black king can't capture it or escape.

u1-l12-s03.hint: The rook goes up the a-file.

u1-l12-s04.hint: Put the queen where your king protects it.

u1-l12-s05.hint: One rook seals off rank 7; the other gives check on rank 8.

u1-l12-s06.explanation: The king can go to d7, e7 or f7.
